summary:
Catch per unit effort standardises catch by how hard you fished: fish per hour, per hundred hooks, per trawl. It returns catch per unit effort, change in CPUE and implied annual change, and the panel shows all of them at once.

It is the classic index of abundance, and comparing it over seasons or years is how a decline is detected before a stock collapses. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Catch Per Unit Effort
sections.html:
CPUE = catch ÷ effort; change (%) = (CPUE_now − CPUE_before) ÷ CPUE_before × 100

sections.title: How do I use the Catch Per Unit Effort?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: catch of 340 individuals, effort of 40 hours, cpue in an earlier survey of 12 /hour.

Substituting them into the formula gives catch per unit effort of 8.5 /hour, change in cpue of -29.17%, implied annual change of -5.83 %/year.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• CPUE is assumed proportional to abundance; that assumption fails when fishers concentrate on the last remaining shoals, so catchability rises as the stock falls.

  • Always state the effort unit. A vessel that doubles its gear changes CPUE without any change in the fish.

  • The percentage change divided by the number of years gives a rough annual rate; a proper series needs a regression of log CPUE against time.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Comparing CPUE across different gear, seasons or vessels.
  • Reporting catch totals and calling them CPUE.
  • Fitting a trend to two points.

faq.q: Why is CPUE used instead of total catch?
faq.a: Because total catch mixes abundance with effort — more boats catch more fish even when the stock is unchanged.
CPUE staying high while abundance falls, because fishers learn where the remaining fish are.

faq.q: What does the Catch Per Unit Effort actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns catch per unit effort, change in CPUE and implied annual change. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
